How aromatherapy fits into your routine

Practical uses, clear guidance, and conservative safety practices — no grand medical promises, just well-informed support.

Accessible rituals

Simple applications you can keep on the nightstand, in a purse, or at your desk.

Personalized choices

Blends are adjusted for sensitivity, preference, and home environment.

Clear safety guidance

Dilution ratios, patch-test steps, and pet- & pregnancy-aware notes are provided with every blend.

Immediate takeaways

Roll-ons, small sample bottles, and straightforward directions you can start using right away.

How a typical session flows

1

Connect

Share your preferences, routines, sensitivities, and any household considerations (pets, pregnancy, medication — purely informational).

2

Consult

We review safe options, suggested dilutions, and delivery formats (diffuser, roll-on, spray).

3

Blend

A small, tailored blend is prepared; a sample is included so you can try it at home and report back.

4

Support

Receive written notes for use, storage, and dilution — safety steps like patch tests and storage tips are included.

Questions people ask

What dilution ratios do you recommend?
Dilution depends on the product and use. Typical topical dilutions range from 0.5–3% for roll-ons and short-term topical use. Your practitioner will suggest a conservative ratio based on age, sensitivity, and context.
How do I do a patch test?
Apply a small diluted amount to an inner forearm and wait 24 hours. If redness, itching, or irritation appears, discontinue use and contact your practitioner.
Are essential oils safe around pets?
Many oils can affect animals. We use pet-aware guidance and recommend keeping diffusers on low, ensuring ventilation, and avoiding direct topical application to pets. Always consult a veterinarian for concerns.
What about pregnancy and breastfeeding?
We take pregnancy and breastfeeding very seriously. Some oils are not recommended; we select options and dilutions that prioritize safety and may defer use when appropriate.
